title: Seeds, Storms and Restored Lives
overview: Jesus teaches about the different ways people respond to God's message, then shows power over a storm, evil spirits, long illness and even death.

parts.label: Women who supported Jesus (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: Jesus traveled with the Twelve and a group of women he had healed, who paid for the work out of their own money. Mary Magdalene, probably named for the town of Magdala, had been freed from "seven demons", likely meaning a severe affliction, and nothing in the text links her to the sinful woman of the previous chapter, as later tradition did.

parts.label: Four kinds of soil (vv. 4-15)
parts.note: The seed is God's message, and the soils are listeners: some never let it in, some start eagerly but quit under pressure, some are crowded out by worry, money and pleasure, and some hold on and grow. Verse 10 echoes the prophet Isaiah and is hard to read, and interpreters are unsure whether parables hide truth on purpose or simply sort out who wants to look closer.

parts.label: Lamp and true family (vv. 16-21)
parts.note: Jesus says his teaching is meant to come into the open like a lamp on a stand, so how people listen matters: those who take it in gain more, and those who don't lose even what they thought they had. When his mother and brothers arrive, he says his family is everyone who hears God's word and acts on it.

parts.label: Calming the storm (vv. 22-25)
parts.note: A sudden storm nearly swamps the boat while Jesus sleeps, and at the disciples' cry he orders the wind and waves to stop. Many readers connect this to the Hebrew scriptures, where God is the one who rules wind and sea, and the story ends on the disciples' frightened question, "Who is this?"

parts.label: The man called Legion (vv. 26-39)
parts.note: Across the lake, in an area where pigs were kept and so likely mostly non-Jewish, Jesus frees a man living naked among tombs, whose name "Legion" (a Roman army unit of thousands) suggests how many spirits held him, and the spirits enter a herd of pigs that rush into the lake and drown. The frightened locals ask Jesus to leave, while the healed man is sent home to tell what God has done for him.

parts.label: A woman and a girl (vv. 40-56)
parts.note: A woman ill with bleeding for twelve years secretly touches Jesus' cloak and is healed, and he draws her out, calls her "daughter" and says her faith has made her well. Meanwhile Jairus' twelve year old daughter dies, but Jesus takes her hand and raises her, then tells them to give her food and keep it quiet.

disagreement: Christians differ on how to read verse 10 at the heart of the sower parable: whether God deliberately hides understanding from some people, or whether parables simply reveal a closed attitude that was already there.
think: When an idea challenges you, what tends to keep it from taking root: distraction, pressure from others, or something else?
